title: C1126 — Right-hand front side marker lamp connector
introduction:
A little marker lamp still needs an orderly electrical address book. I start with the connector identification table, use the harness heading to select the drawing, then match its cavity labels to the circuit rows. That connects the housing reference to the ground and park-lamp circuit descriptions without guessing from appearance alone.

This page explains the reference fields and their relationships. Access, connector release, physical viewing direction, test conditions and repair methods belong to the matching service procedure. The gauge convention and Box, Size and Used codes are undefined here, so they cannot establish wire selection, dimensions or a test result.

edits.why: The drawing has a rounded outer housing, an upper rectangular feature and side-by-side cavity labels. I use those features to keep the printed view recognizable while matching labels to rows. The harness identifier and housing entry tie the illustration to this reference; the drawing alone does not establish a physical release movement or probing direction.

Each row joins a cavity label to its circuit identifier, wire-color code, gauge entry, function and terminal reference. The functions distinguish the ground return from the park-lamp relay circuit. A relay is an electrically controlled switch, but that function label does not establish that a separate plug-in relay is fitted or where it would be located. These rows describe connections without declaring either path healthy.

Use the kit entry to connect the identification table with its service-parts row, then distinguish the service identifier from the engineering shell identifier. Keep the pigtail's gauge and material fields separate from the original circuit-wire entries; their different roles do not establish a replacement-wire rule. The named image file is a catalog reference, and the row supplies no splicing or installation method.
